To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ERP wave, except the P2 amplitude, decreases with age; category induction elicits greater fronto-central N250 and late positive components in both children and adults, and the N250 component is more lateralized to the left hemisphere in young children but not lateralized in young adults.

(a) the N2 amplitude increased during category induction and decreased with age; (b) the late positive component amplitude increased during category-induction, but decreased with age; and (c) the difference wave suggested that the left hemisphere was more involved in category induction in children than in adults.
the N2 and P3 waves were larger during induction tasks than during non-induction tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of category induction in children and adults.
the development of the neural mechanisms underlying category induction.
how category induction is reflected in electrophysiological responses and how it is related to age.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
children and adults use different neural systems for category induction.
category induction in both children and adults is associated with the N2 component, which is modulated by age, task condition and hemispheric asymmetry.
category induction in children is associated with a larger N2 component and a larger P3 component than in adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
category induction in children is more dependent on frontal and left-hemisphere activity, while in adults category induction is more dependent on posterior and bilateral activity.
category induction in children is associated with the frontal lobe, whereas in adults it is associated with both frontal and parietal lobes.

category induction in children is associated with a larger N2 component and a larger late positive component, whereas in adults, the late positive component is the only ERP component that is associated with category induction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N2 component, which reflects the conflict monitoring process, may be useful in understanding the cognitive mechanisms involved in category induction.
the neural substrates of category induction in children and adults are similar, but that they are different in terms of amplitude and laterality.
category induction is a complex process involving multiple brain areas.
